subject: HarborTech on-site cluster: rack assignments, node roles, and retention map
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Norton <alex.norton@harbortech.com>; Sasha Li <sasha.li@harbortech.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HarborTech on-site cluster: rack assignments, node roles, and retention map

Alex / Sasha —

Thanks for the intake call earlier. Per our notes Ive pulled together the first-pass mapping for the on-site cluster footprint and a proposed ownership/retention model. The goal here is to lock the rack/node allocation and persistent volume retention tiers so procurement can finalize parts and we can book the field install window (week of Oct 12).

High-level asks from HarborTech:
- 3 racks in Rack Room B (2x GPU racks + 1x management/storage)
- Separate encrypted blockstore for model weights (LUNs exported over iSCSI)
- 2 node classes: gpu-large (A6000 equivalent) and compute-small (for preprocessing/serving helper pods)
- 30d hot retention for model-serving PVs, 365d for archived weights (cold)

What Im proposing (attached: rack-map-v2.png, site-inventory-20260907.csv, pv-profiles-v1.xlsx):
- Rack 1 (GPU-1): 12 x gpu-large, NVMe local caching enabled, PV class: gp-fast (30d)
- Rack 2 (GPU-2): 12 x gpu-large, same profile, dedicated NFS export for checkpoint archiver (write-heavy)
- Rack 3 (Mgmt+Storage): 6 x compute-small, SAN controllers for blockstore; blockstore presents two LUN sets: weights-hot (replicated, 30d) and weights-cold (replicated, 1y, snapshot schedule weekly)

Operational notes / constraints:
- We must enforce pod anti-affinity for model replicas across GPU racks to reduce correlated failures.
- KV cache will be sticky to the pod; recommend smallest cache TTL 2h to balance warmup costs.
- Eviction policy: critical-serving pods should be PDB-backed; noncritical batch jobs can be preempted during maintenance.

Action items for us / ask to HarborTech:
1) Confirm rack power PDUs and per-rack PDU redundancy (2N vs N+1).
2) Confirm iSCSI zoning and whether HarborTech wants HSM-managed KMS (their preference noted on call was customer KMS).
3) Approve retention windows in the PV profiles spreadsheet (I put defaults but we can shorten if storage budget constrained).

If that aligns Ill circulate a final acceptance doc for procurement sign-off and schedule a field inventory visit with Marissa and Vanessa.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
email: michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HarborTech on-site cluster: rack assignments, node roles, and retention map

Michael —

Thanks for the summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side after reviewing the attachments:
1) For Rack 3 SAN controllers: can Redwoods installer test failover with our backup controller during acceptance? Wed like to see an automated failover before sign-off.
2) weights-hot LUN: can you confirm the expected IOPS baseline youre using to size gp-fast? We currently have a rough budget for 25k IOPS across the cluster but havent allocated per-LUN.
3) KMS: we prefer HarborTech-managed KMS in our VPC (we will provide a key policy). Wed also like to keep HSM option open for the future.

Well review with facilities on PDU redundancy and get back by EOD Friday. Otherwise this looks reasonable.

Best,
Alex Norton
VP, Infrastructure | HarborTech
alex.norton@harbortech.com | +1 617-555-0199

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Norton <alex.norton@harbortech.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HarborTech on-site cluster: rack assignments, node roles, and retention map

Alex / team —

Responding to Alexs points and adding engineering details for acceptance testing:

1) SAN failover: yes, we can include a scripted failover test in the install validation checklist. Installer will perform controller cutover and issue a controlled IO workload (fio profile included in attachments) to validate reconvergence. Well capture timings and any resync alerts in the final report.

2) IOPS sizing: gp-fast baseline I used in pv-profiles-v1.xlsx assumes 10k IOPS per GPU rack for weights-hot LUN distribution (assuming NVMe caching absorbs small random reads). If HarborTech wants to target 25k cluster-wide, we should re-balance to 12k/13k across the two GPU racks; that would need an upgraded SAN disk tier or additional LUN spindles.

3) KMS integration: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS; well need the key ARN and a temporary test key to validate mount-time decryption in the preflight environment. HSM readiness is a separate step; recommend capturing that as an upgrade ticket but not gating initial install.

4) Node eviction / QoS: recommend reserving 10% CPU and 4Gi RAM on all gpu-large nodes for kubelet eviction buffer and driver daemons. Also marking the preemptible batch instance class (compute-small) for any cost-bound workloads.

Ive attached a short acceptance checklist (installer-acceptance-checklist.md) and an updated fio profile (fio-weights-hot.job) to the drive link.

Next steps proposed:
- HarborTech confirms PDU redundancy + IOPS target (Alex) by Fri 11 Sep
- Redwood to update pv profile and final rack BOM by Mon 14 Sep (Marissa to lead procurement doc)
- Field install window: provisionally Oct 12-15; Marissa and Vanessa to schedule on-site logistics after BOM sign-off.

Fyi: tagging Marissa for procurement lead and Vanessa for install coordination.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Staff Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Michael
